theme: wildcard: an events and shocks analyst (World Cup 2026, hurricanes, wi
queries_run: gh search repos "FIFA World Cup 2026 schedule" --limit 40
gh search repos "labor action tracker strikes" --limit 40

note: WebSearch site:github.com queries were blocked session-wide (budget exhausted at 200/200) before any of this scout's searches ran; relied on gh search repos (5 calls, used up budget) + WebFetch on known/likely repo URLs and github.com/topics pages instead

candidates.name: World-Cup-2026-Schedule-Calendar
candidates.what_it_holds: Interactive FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture list (64 matches, 16 host cities across US/Canada/Mexico, Jun-Jul 2026) with an auto-updating WebCal/iCal subscription feed -- machine-readable match dates/venues, MIT licensed.
candidates.why_useful: Gives exact match dates and host-city assignments (several overlap ABNB's top-13 Inside Airbnb markets: LA, NYC metro via nearby, Mexico City) to build city-level demand-shock dummies for the 3Q26 nights nowcast and regional mix during the World Cup window already inside the current data panel.

candidates.name: fwc26
candidates.what_it_holds: Live FIFA World Cup 2026 schedule, scores, standings, knockout bracket, host-city profiles and stadium weather in local timezone; actively updated as of 14 Sep 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Host-city profiles + stadium-level data could be repurposed as a per-city event calendar (attendance size proxies, dates) for regressing nights/ADR spikes in host markets during the tournament quarter.

candidates.name: world-cup-2026-agent-skill
candidates.what_it_holds: Packaged "skill" bundling FIFA World Cup 2026 schedule/results/standings/venue/bracket data for AI-agent consumption -- effectively a structured JSON of matches and venues intended to be machine-queried.
candidates.why_useful: If it bundles a static JSON schedule (host city, date, kickoff time) it is a lightweight, no-scrape source of the same event-calendar dummy variable as the other WC26 repos, packaged for programmatic reuse.

candidates.name: hurdat2
candidates.what_it_holds: R package to read and analyze NOAA's HURDAT2 Atlantic/East-Pacific hurricane best-track dataset (storm name, date/time, lat/lon, max wind, pressure, category, for every storm since 1851/1949) directly from the NHC text feed into tidy tables.
candidates.why_useful: Landfall dates/locations/intensity for Q3/Q4 hurricane season (peak Aug-Oct, inside the pitch's forecast quarters) let the team build Florida/Caribbean/Gulf-market booking-disruption and cancellation dummies, and back-test past hurricane quarters against Inside-Airbnb-covered markets (New Orleans is in the 13-city panel).
candidates.size_hint: small package, pulls a public text feed (no committed data), full historical span

candidates.name: Hurdat2Converter
candidates.what_it_holds: Script converting NOAA's raw HURDAT2 fixed-format text file into a clean, analysis-ready CSV/table (storm id, date, position, wind, pressure).
candidates.why_useful: Alternative lightweight tool to the R package above for the same hurricane best-track series, useful if the team's pipeline is Python-only.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: duplicate function of BigelowLab/hurdat2, different language

candidates.name: disasters (replication package)
candidates.what_it_holds: Full replication package for an academic paper measuring economic disruption from climate disasters: cross-references the EM-DAT global disaster database against MODIS burned-area satellite data and IBTrACS wind-field data, with a 1,174-row register linking every number in the paper to its source (code + data + provenance register).
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made, point-in-time-conscious linkage of EM-DAT (global disaster event records: type, country, date, deaths, damages) to MODIS/IBTrACS -- gives the team a vetted way to pull EM-DAT-quality disaster events (wildfires, storms, floods) by country/date for building an events-and-shocks regressor without re-deriving the EM-DAT extract from scratch, and models exactly the kind of selection/measurement bias (what gets recorded vs. not) that matters if disaster counts are used as a KPI driver.
candidates.time_coverage: not fully specified, multi-decade (EM-DAT/MODIS/IBTrACS overlap era)

candidates.name: thesis-flood-impact-analysis-2025
candidates.what_it_holds: MS thesis codebase measuring flood-disaster impacts by combining MODIS satellite imagery, climate data, and EM-DAT disaster records; includes a processing pipeline that pulls and cleans EM-DAT flood events.
candidates.why_useful: Working EM-DAT extraction/cleaning code (flood subtype) that could be adapted to pull other disaster types (storm, wildfire) by country/date for an events regressor; illustrates how to join disaster events to a market panel.

candidates.name: python-aio-georss-gdacs
candidates.what_it_holds: Async Python library that pulls the live GDACS (Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System) GeoRSS feed -- real-time global disaster alerts (earthquakes, cyclones, floods, volcanoes, droughts) with severity/alert-level, location, and date.
candidates.why_useful: GDACS is a genuinely global, near-real-time, free disaster feed (UN/EU backed) broader than EM-DAT's slower-updated historical archive; a lightweight client makes it feasible to build a live events-and-shocks flag feeding the nights/ADR nowcast for the current quarter, not just backtests.
candidates.size_hint: small library, live feed (no historical archive bundled)

candidates.name: perimeter
candidates.what_it_holds: Tracks California wildfire perimeters from CAL FIRE's FRAP historical fire-perimeter database and CAL FIRE's DINS damage-inspection dataset (structure-level damage assessments) -- geospatial fire-extent polygons plus damage records.
candidates.why_useful: California is one of ABNB's larger single-country revenue pools and hosts several Inside-Airbnb-panel markets (LA, San Diego); fire perimeter + date + damage-inspection data would let the team flag wildfire-season demand/cancellation shocks to West Coast STR nights and ADR by market and date.
candidates.size_hint: unofficial beta, actively updated (last commit 13 Sep 2026)
candidates.time_coverage: historical FRAP perimeters + current DINS inspections

candidates.name: backburner
candidates.what_it_holds: R utilities for collecting open US wildfire data plus matched climate features (weather station data joined to fire events).
candidates.why_useful: Alternative/older tooling for assembling a US wildfire event panel with weather covariates, useful if the team wants wildfire dates outside California too (e.g., Pacific Northwest markets not yet in the Inside Airbnb panel).

candidates.name: holidays (Open World Holidays Framework)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library programmatically generating official government (and financial-market) holidays for 250 country/subdivision codes, with state/province-level subdivisions for many countries; can export as .ics calendars; MIT licensed, 1.9k stars, actively maintained (4,066 commits).
candidates.why_useful: Precise, code-verifiable public-holiday calendars by country and subdivision are a direct input to seasonal demand and party-size modeling (idea #20 in CONTEXT.md gap list touches length-of-stay/seasonality) and to building holiday-adjusted nights nowcasts across all of ABNB's regional splits (NA/EMEA/LatAm/APAC), not just the US.
candidates.size_hint: small library, generates data programmatically (no storage limit)

candidates.name: Nager.Date
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-source public-holiday data and a free REST API (nagerholidays.com/api/v3) covering 200+ countries; holiday objects carry date, local/English name, country code, subdivision, and type (Public/Bank/School/Authorities/Optional/Observance); MIT licensed, 1.4k stars, 1,706 commits, also ships as NuGet/Docker.
candidates.why_useful: A second, independently maintained global holiday source (cross-check against `holidays`/vacanza) with a live queryable API -- useful for point-in-time holiday-calendar snapshots by country for the seasonality/party-size and regional-mix work, and distinguishes School holidays specifically (relevant to family/group travel timing).
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps vacanza/holidays; keep both as independent cross-checks

candidates.name: passport-index-dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Visa-requirement matrix for 199 passports x 199 destination countries, 2019-2025, in six files (three matrix + three tidy/long formats, ISO-2/ISO-3/full-name keyed); values are visa-free days, visa-on-arrival, eTA, e-visa, visa-required, or no-admission; sourced from passportindex.org; MIT licensed; archived Jan 2025 (successor data referenced as living elsewhere from Feb 2026).
candidates.why_useful: A time-stamped (near point-in-time, annual snapshots 2019-2025) global visa-policy panel is exactly the "visa changes" shock category in the brief -- lets the team flag bilateral visa-requirement changes (e.g., a source country gaining/losing visa-free access to a destination) that would shift cross-border nights and regional mix, and is structured for a difference-in-differences design around policy-change dates.
candidates.size_hint: small, 6 CSV files, 199x199 matrices across 7 annual vintages

candidates.name: Passport-Index-Dataset (alsonpr fork/rebuild)
candidates.what_it_holds: Independently collected dataset from the Passport Power Index with visa-requirement information by country pair.
candidates.why_useful: Alternative/cross-check source for the same visa-requirement panel as ilyankou's dataset, useful if vintages or coverage differ.

candidates.name: indice-movilidad-visamundial
candidates.what_it_holds: A Spanish-language global visa-mobility index covering visa requirements for 199 passports against 199 destinations, with an explicit Latin America focus, CC-BY 4.0 licensed, updated August 2026.
candidates.why_useful: More recently updated (Aug 2026, vs. the archived Jan 2025 ilyankou set) and LatAm-focused visa dataset -- directly useful for the LatAm regional-mix forecast (Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Argentina inbound/outbound visa-policy shifts named in gap #7) and freely licensed (CC-BY) unlike most competitors.

candidates.name: TC-Viz
candidates.what_it_holds: Tropical cyclone track visualization tool built on IBTrACS (International Best Track Archive for Climate Stewardship) global storm-track data -- the worldwide counterpart to HURDAT2, covering all ocean basins (Atlantic, Pacific, Indian Ocean).
candidates.why_useful: IBTrACS is the global (not just Atlantic) best-track archive, so a working client extends the hurricane/typhoon shock analysis to APAC markets (Japan, Philippines, Southeast Asia) named in the regional gap list, where HURDAT2 has no coverage.
candidates.size_hint: small visualization tool, pulls public IBTrACS files

candidates.name: Severe Weather Event Reporter
candidates.what_it_holds: Automated severe-weather event analysis tool generating post-event reports (radar imagery, meteorological analysis, damage assessments) by integrating eight federal data sources including NOAA and NWS, tagged for NOAA's Storm Events Database.
candidates.why_useful: Storm Events Database (tornadoes, severe thunderstorms, floods, winter storms -- broader than just hurricanes) by county/date is a finer-grained US weather-shock source than HURDAT2 alone; this tool's multi-source integration could shortcut assembling a county-level severe-weather panel for market-level demand shocks.

candidates.url: https://github.com/[topic]/flight-delay (DOT-BTS-based repos, e.g. "Airline Flight Delay Intelligence", "US Flight Delay Diagnosis")
candidates.name: DOT BTS on-time-performance derivative projects (multiple)
candidates.what_it_holds: Several student/analyst projects hold static extracts of the US DOT BTS On-Time Performance dataset (millions of US domestic flights, airline, airport, delay cause, cancellation flag) -- one explicitly 6.2M+ flights/14 airlines/628 airports, another 745K flights with weather features.
candidates.why_useful: Flight cancellation/delay rates by airport and date (especially around storms/strikes) are a plausible leading proxy for travel disruption that could depress or reschedule STR bookings in the same markets/weeks -- gap #10 explicitly names BTS T-100/DB1B; these repos hold ready-cleaned subsets that avoid a fresh BTS pull, though none appear point-in-time or updated live.
candidates.size_hint: medium, several-hundred-thousand to multi-million row CSVs
candidates.time_coverage: varies by project, generally recent historical years, static snapshot

candidates.name: mcp-gdacs
candidates.what_it_holds: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server wrapping the GDACS global disaster feed, exposing disaster-alert queries as tools callable by an LLM agent.
candidates.why_useful: Lets an LLM-based research agent query live global disaster alerts (type, severity, country, date) programmatically as part of an automated events-and-shocks nowcast pipeline, rather than one-off scraping -- a tooling accelerant for gap #11.

notes: Ten wildcard ideas hunted (events/shocks lens, deliberately non-Airbnb-named): (1) FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture/host-city calendars -- HIT, several MIT-licensed schedule repos with clean date/venue data for the 3Q26 host-city demand-shock dummy; all are hobby trackers, none carry historical attendance or hotel-occupancy overlays, so the team still has to join dates to its own market panel. (2) HURDAT2 Atlantic hurricane best-track data -- HIT, at least two working wrappers (BigelowLab/hurdat2, KameronTH/Hurdat2Converter) pulling NOAA's canonical feed; good for Gulf/Caribbean/Florida landfall dummies in peak hurricane season which falls inside 3Q/4Q26. (3) Global wildfire perimeter/incident data (CAL FIRE/NIFC) -- HIT for California specifically (ChelseaKR/perimeter, actively updated 13 Sep 2026, ties fire perimeters to CAL FIRE DINS damage inspections); no comparable committed dataset found yet for other US wildfire-prone regions (PNW, Mediterranean Europe, Australia) beyond the smaller/stale `backburner` repo -- worth a dedicated follow-up search for NIFC/EFFIS mirrors. (4) EM-DAT global disaster database -- MISS as a raw open mirror (EM-DAT itself requires registration and is not redistributed wholesale on GitHub) but HIT as embedded data inside academic replication packages (andreiosiptsov/disasters, nicolejkeeney thesis) that include working EM-DAT extraction/cleaning code -- a follow-up agent should try those repos' data folders directly rather than searching for "EM-DAT dataset" generically. (5) Strike/labor-action trackers (Cornell ILR Labor Action Tracker or similar) -- MISS; GitHub's own "labor-action-tracker" topic is empty and no mirror of the Cornell ILR dataset (which itself is not freely bulk-downloadable) turned up; a follow-up agent should try WebSearch (once budget resets) for "Cornell ILR Labor Action Tracker" bulk data / API, and separately search for European strike databases (ETUI, Eurofound) mirrors. (6) Visa/entry-policy change trackers -- HIT, strong: ilyankou/passport-index-dataset (199x199 matrix, 2019-2025, MIT) plus a more recently updated LatAm-focused CC-BY alternative (josegaspard/indice-movilidad-visamundial, Aug 2026); both are annual snapshots, not true point-in-time daily vintages, so exact policy-change dates would still need cross-referencing against news/IATA Timatic changelogs. (7) Public holiday / school calendar datasets -- HIT, strong: vacanza/holidays (250 country codes, subdivisions, MIT, 1.9k stars) and nager/Nager.Date (200+ countries, live API, distinguishes School vs Public holidays) are both mature, actively maintained, and complementary cross-checks -- probably the single most "ready to use today" find in this scout run. (8) Concert/tour and major-event calendars (Bandsintown/Songkick/Ticketmaster aggregators) -- WEAK HIT; found only small personal-use scrapers/notifiers (a few stars each, e.g. the Dutch "Buitenlandse Concerten Grabber" pulling Bandsintown+Songkick+Setlist.fm) with no committed historical dataset and uncertain licensing/ToS status for the underlying platforms -- flagged as method-only, not verified further per the no-scrape rule. (9) Earthquake catalogs (USGS) -- not directly searched this run (ran out of the 5 gh-search budget and WebSearch was already exhausted before this scout started); a follow-up agent should check github.com/topics/usgs-earthquake and the well-known USGS earthquake GeoJSON feed wrapper libraries. (10) Flight cancellation/delay databases (DOT BTS / Eurocontrol) tied to storms/strikes -- HIT but weak: several student ML projects hold static DOT BTS on-time-performance extracts (up to 6.2M flights) with delay-cause and cancellation fields, but none are live, point-in-time, or already joined to storm/strike dates -- would need the team to do that join itself; no Eurocontrol equivalent found this run. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this session's shared WebSearch budget (200/200) was already exhausted before any of scout #259's own searches executed, so every WebSearch call in this run returned zero results; all findings above came from `gh search repos` (all 5 calls used) plus WebFetch against known/likely repo URLs and GitHub topic pages, which is a narrower discovery method than free-text web search -- a follow-up agent with a fresh WebSearch budget should re-run ideas #5, #8, #9 and add explicit EM-DAT/GDACS/IBTrACS/Eurocontrol mirror searches, since topic-page browsing under-samples repos that never tagged themselves with the right GitHub topic.
